## Controlled h215 topology comparison: historical W and new D

This separate comparison adds two accepted D observations to the nine-observation warehouse-only scalability cohort above. W forbids direct origin-to-customer arcs; D permits them in addition to warehouse-mediated routes. The same frozen h215 input, 215-member population, common OD/DC/DD arcs, costs, indexed penalties, original DET arrays and nine equiprobable STO scenarios were checked. D adds 592 OC arcs and 35,520 DET/319,680 STO flow variables. Both use four solver threads and a global 14,400-second ceiling per arm, MIPGap=0.01 and the same scientific implementation. W job2217990 is a historical control, not a contemporaneous runtime replicate.

| Mode/topology | Objective, BRL trillion | Economic subtotal, BRL billion | Gap, % | Native Runtime, min | Domestic service, % |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DET W | 11.437342 | 389.810 | 0.000812 | 2.04 | 91.861 |
| DET D | 7.340492 | 338.715 | 0.552427 | 1.73 | 89.896 |
| STO W | 13.071397 | 393.902 | 0.740159 | 40.76 | 92.267 |
| STO D | 7.355002 | 340.109 | 0.623718 | 43.04 | 89.857 |

: Original validated h215 W/D observations. Optimal native status means the configured gap criterion, not exact zero-gap optimality. {#tbl-wd-h215}

The returned D penalized objectives are 35.82% lower in DET and 43.73% lower in STO. D incumbents are below the corresponding W lower bounds, supporting strict penalized-objective improvement under the checked network/cost conditions. The bound intervals bracket the exact penalized-optimum reduction at 35.819–36.175% (DET) and 43.313–44.083% (STO), conditional on the retained valid bounds. These are mathematical bounds, not statistical confidence intervals.

The economic subtotals of the returned plans are 13.11%/13.66% lower, but the optimizer does not minimize that subtotal alone. Domestic service falls from 91.861% to 89.896% in DET and from 92.267% to 89.857% in STO; expected total shortage increases from 55.16 to 68.48 million tonnes and from 52.40 to 68.74 million tonnes, respectively. D sharply reduces reception/storage exceedance penalties while allowing a different shortage trade-off. Lower penalized cost is therefore not improved service, no-slack feasibility or an investment recommendation.

Direct routes account for 82.17%/81.81% of expected OC+DC destination arrivals in DET/STO, not of all produced grain or distinct network-arc movements. All 69 candidates still receive positive capacity. Positive expansion occurs at 142 sites in each D plan, versus 80/75 in W; bulkification falls from 66/71 sites to four. The returned hub-location decisions remain distributed, not a sparse few-hub network.

D has more variables: 1,597,694 DET and 14,374,334 STO, compared with 1,562,174/14,054,654 in W. Native runtimes are 103.93/2,582.59 seconds in D versus 122.51/2,445.52 in W. Different attained gaps, historical timing, a single observation per cell and uncontrolled shared-system effects preclude causal speedup or a universal complexity claim. Artificial penalties remain about 95.39%/95.38% of D totals. Their unchanged weights influence routing, investments, relaxation/search and the reported penalized gap; a 1% total gap is not a 1% economic-subtotal or service certificate.

Original validation and owned-step/phase/terminal receipts close both D arms. Portable review replays those archived receipts, not a fresh private-input residual re-solve. No additional solve or repetition is required to close this bounded h215 W/D phase. Original h500/S5 is now accepted and closed; the separate SCIP test, integrated coauthor review and S6-B remain open.
